hero.title: Type conversion & parsing
intro.0: Data rarely arrives in the type you need - text has to become a number, a number has to become text, a decimal has to lose its fraction. These are the conversions you reach for every day. You write each one and run it.
task.1.title: Text into a number
task.1.context:
Data often arrives as **text** - a form field, a line from a file. Before you can do maths with it, you turn it into a number. `int.Parse("3")` reads the text `"3"` and hands back the number `3`.

Write a `Kitten` whose `AgeNextYear(string ageText)` parses the age and returns it plus one.
task.1.goal.0: Give `Kitten` an `int AgeNextYear(string ageText)` that parses `ageText` and returns it plus 1.
task.2.title: A number into text
task.2.context:
The other direction: turn a number into text so you can build a label or a code. `count.ToString()` gives the digits back as a `string`, ready to join with other text.

Write a `Chip` whose `Code(int n)` returns the letter `"C"` followed by the number as text - so `7` becomes `"C7"`.
task.2.goal.0: Give `Chip` a `string Code(int n)` that returns `"C"` joined with `n` as text.
task.3.title: Drop the decimals
task.3.context:
A `double` like `3.9` carries a fractional part. Casting it with `(int)` **drops** the decimals - it truncates toward zero, it does not round - so `(int)3.9` is `3`, not `4`.

Write a `Scale` whose `Whole(double kg)` returns just the whole-number part of a weight.
task.3.goal.0: Give `Scale` an `int Whole(double kg)` that returns `kg` cast to `int`.
task.4.title: Parse without crashing
task.4.context:
`int.Parse("cat")` throws - the text is not a number, and the program stops. `int.TryParse` is the safe version: it returns a `bool` saying whether it worked, and puts the number into an `out` variable when it does.

Write a `Gate` whose `IsNumber(string text)` returns whether the text is a whole number.
task.4.goal.0: Give `Gate` a `bool IsNumber(string text)` that returns the result of `int.TryParse`.
task.5.title: What you learned
task.5.context: Four everyday conversions - the moves you reach for whenever data crosses a boundary.
task.5.summaryIntro: Values change type constantly: text comes in, numbers go out, decimals need trimming. You wrote each conversion by hand:
task.5.summaryItems.0.title: Text to a number -
task.5.summaryItems.0.text: `int.Parse("3")` reads text and gives back the number `3`, so you can do maths with it.
task.5.summaryItems.1.title: A number to text -
task.5.summaryItems.1.text: `n.ToString()` turns a number into its digits as a `string`, ready to join into a label or code.
task.5.summaryItems.2.title: Drop the decimals -
task.5.summaryItems.2.text: `(int)3.9` casts a `double` to `int` by truncating - it drops the fraction, it does not round.
task.5.summaryItems.3.title: Parse without crashing -
task.5.summaryItems.3.text: `int.TryParse` returns a `bool` for whether the text was a number, instead of throwing when it is not.
task.5.summaryClose: Reach for `TryParse` over `Parse` whenever the text might be wrong - the same double/string/int conversions carry over to every type you will meet next.
concept.pr-parse.def: Reading a value out of text - int.Parse("3") turns the text into the number 3.
concept.pr-to-string.def: Turning a value into its text form, so a number can be joined into a label or code.
concept.pr-cast.def: Converting a value to another type with (int) - casting a double to int drops the fraction rather than rounding.
concept.pr-try-parse.def: The safe parse: it returns a bool for success and writes the number through an out parameter instead of crashing on bad text.
